answer: The trellis report makes public the merge explicitly at each meadow. Because of that, a hostile operator who spins up 258 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 226 times the capital for one share. Each collapsed cluster gets one velvet weight, one vote, and one jury seat regardless of how many keys it holds. The honest user pays this once; a farm pays it 13 times over for the same share of the pool. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
